Highlight · Feature Tour

Everything Highlight can do.

A walkthrough of the whole feature set. Every screenshot on this page is the real interface, and every tooltip and notification below is the live thing rendered by the extension's own stylesheet — not a picture of one.

Everything here is live in v2.3.1
Lists

Your watchlist, organised

As many lists as you want, each with its own colour, text colour and weight. Group them into folders, drag to reorder, filter by name, and pause one without deleting it.

Badges say what a list does at a glance — whether it has a tooltip, an alert, a link, a match limit, or is muted.

Choose the row icons. Which actions appear on each row, and in what order, is configurable.

Whole-word or partial per list, plus case sensitivity and multi-word phrases — where the longer phrase always wins over a shorter one inside it.

On the page

The invoice from Northwind Trading is still overdue, and Case No. 40912 has not been closed. Escalate to Compliance before Friday.

Four different lists and one pattern rule, all marking the same sentence at once. This is the real highlight styling, running on this page.

Tooltips

Context, right where the word is

Attach a note to a whole list, or to one specific word inside it. Hover to see it, or click to pin it open; Escape dismisses every pinned tooltip at once.

Always-visible mode keeps a tooltip open without hovering, and a small corner badge marks the words that have one.

A copy button can be added to any tooltip, and the size and font size are adjustable.

Ten built-in styles, plus any preset you save yourself. Use the arrows to step through all ten.

Tooltip styles 1 / 10
Notifications

A heads-up when a match appears

Turn notifications on for any list and get a toast the moment it matches, with a countdown bar showing how long it will stay.

Position, size, duration and sound are all configurable, and there are ten sounds to choose from.

Or use a native system notification instead of the in-page toast.

Mute without disabling. A muted list keeps highlighting and keeps counting for the inactivity report — it just stays quiet.

Notification styles 1 / 9

Tuned in Settings

The notification panel previews the style live as you change it, so you can see the sound, position and duration you are choosing before anything fires on a real page.

Word rules

Override one word inside a list

A word rule takes a single word out of its list's shared behaviour and gives it its own. The rest of the list is untouched.

ListBilling termsWordauto-renewal
Tooltip60-day notice window — check the termination clause.
Linkopens the playbook in a new window
Scopeonly on *.contracts.example.com

Each word rule carries its own name, its own site scope, and can be shared on its own as a paste-in code.

Pattern rules

Match a shape, not a list of words

A pattern rule highlights text by its format, so it finds values you could never have written down in advance — every case number, account reference, date or amount on the page.

PatternCase No\.\s*(\d{4,6})
FindsCase No. 40912Case No. 8837Case No. 155029
PatternINV-\d{4}-\d{3,5}
FindsINV-2026-0431INV-2025-11902

A live tester runs the pattern against sample text while you type it and counts the matches.

Capture groups let you highlight just one part of what matched, and a per-page match limit stops a broad pattern taking over.

Its own format, interaction and scope tabs, the same as a list — and a pattern can be used as a condition inside a combination rule.

Combination rules

Fire only when things appear together

A combination rule watches for words from different lists landing on the same page. It has three kinds of condition, and one excluded word is enough to hold the whole rule back.

RequiredNorthwind Tradingoverdue
Any of thesechargebackremittancedispute
None of thesesettledwithdrawn

The rule can carry its own tooltip, anchored to whichever of its words you choose, and it fires once per page rather than once per match.

Conflict detection

Overlaps are caught at save time

When a new list or pattern would match text something else already matches, Highlight says so before you save. It names both sides and the exact words that collided, and asks which one wins.

“Keep both” stops that pair being flagged again, without changing either side.

Every decision is remembered and can be revisited, changed, or cleared entirely.

Every decision, in one place

A dedicated screen lists every pair you have already resolved, with the overlapping text and the priority you chose. Change any of them at any time, or use Forget all decisions to start over.

Settings and theming

Two ways to navigate

Every settings panel switches between a single stacked accordion and a horizontal tab strip. Pick whichever suits how you like to move around, and it applies everywhere.

Dark or light, with every colour in the interface adjustable and ten built-in presets to start from — plus your own, saved and shareable.

Three density modes, border thickness, corner shape, shadow depth, typography, and an optional font override for the whole extension.

Three languages — English, Spanish and Lithuanian — switchable at any time.

Keyboard shortcuts for pausing everything, pausing one tab, and jumping between matches. Off by default.

Matching

How closely a word has to match

Accents are ignored by default, so “e” also finds “é” across Spanish, French, German, Nordic, Slavic, Lithuanian and Russian Cyrillic. On top of that, fuzzy matching catches near-misses on purpose.

Exactonly the word as written
Moderategrey also finds gray, Nothwind still finds Northwind
Broadwider still, for names that arrive misspelt

Separate switches decide whether a fuzzy hit may trigger a word rule or satisfy a combination rule — so it can stay out of the strict paths.

Scope and exclusions. A global never-highlight list of words, plus per-list and site-wide allow and block rules with wildcard domains.

Three page-scan modes. Always watch for changes is the default and catches content the moment it appears; Automatic is lighter; Initial load only is fastest.

Housekeeping

What has gone quiet

The inactivity report sorts every word from longest-unseen to most recently seen, and rolls up word rules, combination rules and entirely dormant lists alongside them. It is the fastest way to clean up a watchlist that has drifted.

Exportable as a real .xlsx file.

The record stays on the device. It describes what this browser has seen, so it is never synced between machines.

Everything else

Right-click to add. Select text on any page, right-click, and add it to an existing or brand-new list without opening the popup.

Clickable matches. A list, word rule or pattern can turn its matches into links, opening in the same tab, a new tab, a new window or a private window.

A match count badge on the toolbar icon, showing how many matches are on the current page.

Share anything. Lists, word rules, combination rules and pattern rules each export as a paste-in code you can hand to someone else.

Backup and import. Everything exports as JSON with a category picker, and an import shows you exactly what will merge, change or be removed before it happens. Imports from two other highlighting tools are detected automatically.

Sync across your devices. On Edge and Firefox your setup follows your own browser account, with anything too large kept on the device and marked local only. It is on by default and can be switched off at any time.

Works inside frames. Embedded content and shadow DOM are covered, and pages that build themselves in stages are re-scanned as they finish.

No servers, no accounts, no analytics. Nothing is sent to the developer at any point.

One thing to know about Chrome

Chrome is still on v2.1.0

Everything above describes v2.3.1, which is what is published on Microsoft Edge Add-ons and Firefox Add-ons today. The Chrome Web Store build is still v2.1.0, and an update is on the way. Until it lands, these parts of the tour are not yet in the Chrome version:

Word rules and pattern rules — both arrived after v2.1.0.

Conflict detection and the conflict decisions screen.

The three-condition combination rules shown above. v2.1.0 has combination rules, but only in their simpler form.

Some of the tooltip and notification styles, the extra sounds, and parts of the theme editor.

The layout switch between the accordion and the horizontal tab strip.

Lists, folders, tooltips, notifications, links, scoping, theming, the inactivity report and import/export all work in v2.1.0. The Chrome changelog is the exact record of what that release contains.

Highlight is a personal project, unaffiliated with any employer. Everything runs locally in your browser.
